clue.text: Father had potato cooked immediately

indicators.note: food that is cooked is worked over, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Dad's spuds were cooked on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like it describes the potato, but it signals the anagram of all fifteen letters of FATHER HAD POTATO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means without hesitation, as quickly as a hat can fall, so it is a synonym for instantly.

clue.text: Mutableness of shifting bilaterality

indicators.note: shifting letters move them about, so the word bilaterality is rearranged

explanation.surface: A dry definition: how changeable two-sided symmetry is.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the quality of being capable of change; a synonym pair.

clue.text: Is rubbish turning up in trunks?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Is there rubbish in the swimming shorts or the car boot?
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunks' suggests luggage or swimwear; here it means human torsos.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk is the body without head or limbs, and the plural Latin form names several such bodies.

clue.text: Seriously stumbling experimentally; not terribly plain

indicators.note: stumbling suggests the letters of experimentally are jumbled
not says some letters are taken away, and terribly says those removed are the word plain in a jumbled form

explanation.surface: Someone tripping over in a lab test, and not very plainly at that.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of EXPERIMENTALLY are exactly the answer plus the letters of PLAIN, so removing PLAIN and shuffling the rest gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriously as an intensifier (seriously good) means very much, to a great degree.

clue.text: Commotion mostly in genuine rejection

indicators.note: in places the shortened commotion word inside the word for genuine

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a fuss is a commotion

explanation.surface: A real fuss kicked up over being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commotion' reads as part of the scene, but a shortened synonym of it sits inside the word for genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no to an offer is a turning-down, a synonym for rejection.

clue.text: Showy sites of entertainment in buildings around America

indicators.note: around says the buildings word goes round the abbreviation for America

parts.note: places can mean buildings or premises

explanation.surface: Flashy venues housed in buildings across America.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture palaces and gin palaces are grand, ornate venues for amusement.

clue.text: Change of direction in organised political group produces unfriendliness

indicators.note: a change of compass direction swaps north for south within the group word

parts.note: a front is a political movement, as in the National Front

explanation.surface: A party making a U-turn gets a cold reception.
explanation.definitionFit: A frosty manner is chilly and cold, so the word means coolness towards someone.

clue.text: Collect short book on very famous plant expert

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: to herd is to gather together, collect
A-list means of top celebrity status

explanation.surface: Gather a brief volume about a celebrated botanist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' looks like gathering plants, but it is a verb to shorten; in a down clue 'on' puts the later pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who grows or sells medicinal herbs is a specialist in plants.

clue.text: Pack maybe last bit of mango into pastry dish

indicators.note: into puts the final letter inside the pastry dish word

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dish

indicators.note: last bit of picks the final letter of mango

explanation.surface: A recipe: maybe pack the last bit of mango into the tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' looks like a verb, but it is a pack of cards; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune-tellers use a deck of special cards, so this is one kind of card pack.

clue.text: Regularly affable leader of crew on line, working with birds

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of affable
leader of takes the first letter of crew

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A friendly foreman on the railway gets on with the pigeons.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport is training hawks to hunt, a craft practised with birds of prey.

clue.text: Severely bruised group accepting deficiency; subsequently dismal

indicators.note: subsequently puts the dismal word after the rest
accepting means the group word takes the deficiency word inside it

parts.note: a band is a group
lack is a deficiency
blue means sad, dismal

explanation.surface: A band short of something ends up gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes skin showing the dark colours of heavy bruising, an idiom for badly beaten.

clue.text: Marauders; horsemen surrounding area

indicators.note: surrounding says the horsemen word goes round the letter for area

parts.note: riders are horsemen

explanation.surface: Marauding horsemen encircle a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name people who attack and plunder; a synonym.

clue.text: Not completely comprehend every cry expressing derision

indicators.note: not completely means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to catch is to grasp or understand
all means every

explanation.surface: Failing to understand every jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill whistle or shout of disapproval from a crowd is a jeer of scorn.

clue.text: Bright display in British lounge

parts.note: to laze is to lounge about

explanation.surface: A colourful show in a British sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' looks like a room, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A blaze of colour is a brilliant show, a fiery burst of light.

clue.text: Equipped and cued actor to dance

indicators.note: making letters dance sets them moving about, so cued actor is rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor, kitted out and given his cue, starts dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be accoutred is to be fitted out with gear or dress, kitted out.

clue.text: Daughter going into revamped classier data storage system

indicators.note: going into puts the letter for daughter inside the rearranged letters
revamped means remade, so the letters of classier are reworked

explanation.surface: A daughter joins a smartened-up, posher setting.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an early optical disc format storing video, a medium for holding data.

clue.text: Brighten up; umpire essentially excuses run blunder

parts.note: a ref is a referee, an umpire

indicators.note: essentially takes the heart of the word, the middle letter of excuses

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
bish is British slang for a mistake

explanation.surface: The umpire basically forgives a running mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is informal British for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate or redecorate a room is to smarten it up, freshen its look.

clue.text: Plucks trimmed, variable, oddly drippy stuff primarily from these bran tubs

indicators.note: trimmed cuts off both ends of plucks, keeping the middle

parts.note: Y is a mathematical variable

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of drippy
primarily takes the first letter of stuff

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out drippy stuff from fairground barrels of bran.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a British fête game: prizes buried in bran to be fished out blind.
explanation.definitionFit: At British fairs a container of bran hiding prizes is the same game as a random grab for a prize.

clue.text: Bury that chap (not husband) in time between events

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: not says the husband letter is left out of the word for that chap

parts.note: him refers to that chap

explanation.surface: Burying a man while his husband is away, in the meantime.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval or meantime is a period separating two happenings.

clue.text: Brag noisily of small bet involving golf

indicators.note: involving means the bet word wraps round the golf letter

parts.note: a wager is a bet
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Loud boasting over a little bet on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger is to boast and show off loudly, swaggering talk being boastful.

clue.text: Crumbly cheese's matte finish partly making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crumbly cheese has a dull finish that is returning to fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek brined white cheese, usually spelt feta, crumbles easily.

clue.text: Announce cut in tense film

indicators.note: in places the cut of meat inside the tense and film letters

parts.note: T is a grammar abbreviation for tense
ET is the Spielberg film
rump is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: Declaring that a scene is cut from a tense movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like an edit, but it is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to proclaim it loudly, as a herald would.

clue.text: Requisition newspapers

definitions.meaning: to commandeer or force into service

explanation.surface: Demand the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to force into service, the other is the print media as a body.

clue.text: Display resistance then help strike

indicators.note: then says the following pieces come next in order

parts.note: to air is to display or show
R is the physics symbol for resistance
aid means help

explanation.surface: Put on a show of defiance, then help the strikers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action; it is a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombing attack from aircraft is a military strike.

clue.text: Region circling new sphere of action

indicators.note: circling means the region word goes round the new letter

parts.note: an area is a region

explanation.surface: A region surrounding a fresh field of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is figuratively a field of activity, as in the political arena.

clue.text: Spooner's at large — trek to find amphibian!

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the first letters of the two words

parts.note: at large means free, on the loose
to trog is British slang for to trudge, trek

explanation.surface: Spooner, out and about, sets off on a hike to find a frog.
explanation.walkthrough: TROG is informal British for a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing frog is an amphibian living among branches.

clue.text: Perfect plan pursued by student

indicators.note: pursued by puts the student letter after the plan word

parts.note: an idea is a plan
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A flawless plan with a student hard on its heels.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is flawless, matching the best conception of it.

clue.text: Stupidly had a ham arms race — somewhat dippy!

indicators.note: stupidly means senselessly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Foolishly someone staged an arms race over a ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat dippy' is an understatement for the idiom's crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes wild craziness, from hares behaving erratically in spring; eccentric.
